discovery: Discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion
motivation: In 2005 the SDSS (Eisenstein et al.) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Percival et al.) teams independently detected the imprint of primordial sound waves, frozen at recombination, in the clustering of galaxies. Eisenstein also developed the theoretical framework that made the feature a precise standard ruler. This detection showed that the acoustic physics seen in the cosmic microwave background survives into the present-day matter distribution, a striking confirmation of gravitational instability in a baryon-dark matter universe. Because the ruler is calibrated by well-understood early-universe physics, it gives a geometric measure of expansion history entirely independent of supernova distances. BAO measurements confirmed cosmic acceleration with completely different systematics. Through BOSS, eBOSS and now DESI, which in 2024-25 reported hints of evolving dark energy, they have become a pillar of precision cosmology and a key test of LambdaCDM.
